old_caption: The video captures a serene sky scene, showcasing the gradual drift of clouds across a vivid blue backdrop. The clouds, appearing as grey and white masses with dark undersides, shift and change shape, creating a sense of slow motion. They drift from left to right across the frame, with no visible characters or animals. The camera remains static, allowing viewers to fully appreciate the tranquil and ever-changing landscape above.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures a serene sky scene, showcasing the dynamic movement of clouds across a vivid blue backdrop. Initially, the sky is filled with fluffy white clouds that gradually shift and change shape, creating a sense of continuous motion. As the video progresses, the clouds begin to thin out, revealing more of the deep blue sky. The clouds transition from dense formations to wispy streaks, adding depth and texture to the scene. The lighting subtly shifts, highlighting the varying densities and colors of the clouds, from bright white to soft gray. Throughout the video, there are no visible characters or animals, focusing solely on the natural beauty of the sky. The camera remains stationary, allowing viewers to fully appreciate the tranquil and ever-changing landscape above.
caption: The video captures a daytime sky with deep blue, a layered gray-and-white cloud bank at lower-left, a faint diagonal wispy band across the right, and scattered top wisps. A small white cumulus puff near upper center becomes more distinct and stays nearly fixed as nearby streaks shift. The left bank changes shape, with brighter white cloud mass extending into upper-left and its right edge protrusion moving modestly. The diagonal cirrus band on the right remains largely fixed, and bottom-right horizon clouds stay largely in place. The differing movements appear as slow drift of separate cloud layers rather than one uniform sweep. A few isolated dark specks appear only briefly and do not form a continuing visible object. The sky is still changing, with the bank continuing its gradual motion and the upper puff slowly evolving.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.

'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
